name: Earringsmaxxing

lead: Earringsmaxxing is the looksmaxxing term for wearing earrings to change how the face, ears and overall style read. A stud or small hoop adds a small point of detail near the face, and users describe it as a way to look more fashionable, edgier or more distinctive.

The idea circulates mainly as a style opinion rather than a researched technique. On looksmax.org, posters disagree on whether earrings raise or lower attractiveness, with some saying they ascend almost anyone and others saying they change the impression toward a particular subculture.

paras: People typically choose a pierced earlobe with a small stud or hoop, or use clip-on and magnetic styles for unpierced ears. Forum users discuss stud versus hoop, metal and placement. Earlobe piercings generally take about 6 to 8 weeks to heal initially.

Piercing complications reported in the literature summarised by Wikipedia include infection, allergic reaction (nickel in particular), keloids and torn lobes; cartilage piercings heal more slowly and carry higher infection risk. Social perception of men's earrings varies by setting and community.

angle.text: Users wear earrings to add a point of detail and personality near the face, much as glasses or a haircut frame it. The effect is a style change that depends on the earring, the face and the setting, and forum members report mixed social reactions.

lead: Earringsmaxxing is a style-focused looksmaxxing term for wearing earrings to alter the appearance of the face and ears. A stud or small hoop draws a small, deliberate focal point to the side of the face, and users treat it as an accessory-level change that can be paired with grooming and clothing.[1][2]

Earrings are among the oldest forms of body adornment, with gold examples from sites such as Ur and Lothal and Minoan hoops from around 2000 to 1600 BCE.[2] Men's earrings spread through countercultures in the late 1960s, were popularised by punk and musicians in the 1980s, and became widely accepted by the early 21st century.[2]

In forum discussion the topic is framed as opinion: one looksmax.org thread asks whether earrings are a legitimate looksmax for a young man whose friends suggested them, and replies range from saying they ascend people to saying they shift the vibe toward a harder or more subcultural image.[1] No studies have examined earrings as a facial-attractiveness modification.

paras: Earrings come as studs, which sit flush on the lobe, hoops, drops and dangles, with clip-on or magnetic versions for ears that are not pierced.[2] In looksmaxxing talk, small studs and simple hoops are the usual subject; one forum reply specifically advises tops (studs) over dangling styles.[1]

Ear piercing is one of the oldest known body modifications. Gold earrings were found at Lothal in India and in the Royal Cemetery at Ur, and Minoan hoop earrings were common between roughly 2000 and 1600 BCE.[2] Earrings were fashionable among English courtiers in the 16th century, and sailors wore them, with a pierced lobe sometimes marking a voyage around the world or across the equator.[2]

In the 20th century piercing declined, then returned in the late 1950s and 1960s. Men's piercing spread through hippie and gay communities in the late 1960s, was popularised by punk and musicians in the 1980s and became broadly accepted in the early 2000s.[2]

The only community material is a looksmax.org thread in which an 18-year-old describes a friend and a girl suggesting earrings and painted nails and asks whether it counts as a legitimate looksmax. One reply says earrings definitely ascend but recommends studs; another says they ascend everyone but give a more 'dark triad' impression and can draw teasing.[1] Users thus treat earrings as a style trade-off between looking more distinctive and signalling a particular image.

Wikipedia summarises a study in which up to 35 percent of people with pierced ears had complications, most commonly infection, then allergic reaction, keloids and tearing; nickel is a significant allergen.[2] Cartilage piercings heal two to three times slower than lobes, and sterilised hollow needles are generally considered safer than piercing guns.[2] Piercers commonly advise wearing earrings continuously for months so the hole does not close.[2]
No studies found. Research on earrings concerns piercing complications and allergy, not their effect on perceived attractiveness.

lore.intro: Earringsmaxxing is discussed on looksmax.org as a low-commitment style change whose social reception is disputed.[1]

claims.claim: Earrings change the vibe toward an edgier image

timeline.event: Men's piercing spreads through hippie and gay communities.[2]
Punk and musicians popularise men's earrings.[2]
